name: Nethaniah
title: Father of Ishmael, the regicide
summary: Nethaniah was a man of royal lineage in Judah, the son of Elishama. He is best known as the father of Ishmael, who murdered Gedaliah, the Babylonian-appointed governor over Judah after the fall of Jerusalem. Through his son Ishmael's actions, Nethaniah's name became linked to one of the most dramatic events following Judah's downfall.

keyEvents.title: Nethaniah's royal lineage
keyEvents.description: Nethaniah was of royal descent, the son of Elishama, which gave his family a prominent position in the kingdom of Judah.

keyEvents.title: Ishmael's revolt against Gedaliah
keyEvents.description: Nethaniah's son Ishmael was sent by Baalis, king of Ammon, to kill the governor Gedaliah at Mizpah, leading to chaos in what remained of Judah.

keyEvents.title: The murder of Gedaliah
keyEvents.description: Ishmael, the son of Nethaniah, killed Gedaliah at a meal in Mizpah, along with Judeans and Chaldeans who were present. This was an event of great political significance.

keyEvents.title: The Massacre of the Pilgrims
keyEvents.description: Nethaniah's son Ishmael also killed seventy pilgrims who came from Shechem, Shiloh, and Samaria, and threw their bodies into a well.

keyEvents.title: Johanan's Pursuit of Ishmael
keyEvents.description: Johanan, the son of Kareah, pursued Ishmael, the son of Nethaniah, after these crimes and rescued the captives Ishmael had taken from Mizpah.

keyEvents.title: The Flight to Egypt
keyEvents.description: After Ishmael's actions, the remaining people, including the prophet Jeremiah, fled to Egypt out of fear of Babylonian revenge—a direct consequence of the Nethaniah family's deeds.
